analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: 1. Identify all visual entities on the whiteboard and verify against the audio transcript: there are two user stick figures on the left (representing Tenants and Customers/Resellers), a CDN layer (CloudFront), S3, AppSync, API Gateway, a single shared Lambda icon, DynamoDB, and SQS. 2. Note that although the base world model listed two Lambda icons and mapped AppSync to ThirdParty, the actual whiteboard clearly shows a single central Lambda icon connected to both AppSync and API Gateway, and AppSync is a valid native AWS service in the vocabulary list. 3. Map the four distinct architectural flows described in the transcript: Flow 0 covers Tenant onboarding via the web wizard (CDN -> AppSync -> Lambda -> SQS -> Lambda -> DynamoDB). Flow 1 covers third-party OTA resellers accessing REST endpoints (CDN -> API Gateway -> Lambda). Flow 2 covers customers browsing static event descriptions and images hosted on S3 (Customer -> CDN -> S3 -> CDN -> Customer). Flow 3 covers dynamic booking and mobile check-in via GraphQL, using both direct DynamoDB resolvers and Lambda resolvers with asynchronous SQS post-processing.

graph.name: Anchor Multi-Tenant Serverless Ticketing Platform
graph.notes: Anchor is a multi-tenant ticketing platform serving over 40 tenants (such as Statue of Liberty cruises, Niagara Falls, Alcatraz Island, and NYC Ferry). It uses a completely serverless architecture with CloudFront, S3, AppSync, API Gateway, Lambda, SQS, and DynamoDB partitioned by tenant.

nodes.name: Tenant
nodes.notes: Platform tenants using a web application wizard to onboard and create events (over 20 new tenants onboarded in 6 months).

nodes.name: Customer / OTA Reseller
nodes.notes: Omnichannel clients including customers on websites, mobile apps, check-in apps, and third-party OTA resellers like Expedia, Viator, or GetYourGuide.

nodes.name: CDN
nodes.notes: Entry point for all client requests, routing traffic to S3 for static content, AppSync for GraphQL, or API Gateway for third-party REST APIs.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Serves as an HTTP server hosting static website content such as ticket offerings, event descriptions, and pictures.

nodes.name: AppSync
nodes.notes: GraphQL gateway using pipeline resolvers to trigger Lambda functions or communicate directly with DynamoDB.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Provides a regular REST endpoint for third-party resellers and OTAs.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Executes business logic across all channels, fans out subroutines to SQS, reprocesses queued messages, and interacts with DynamoDB.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Shared tables across the platform utilizing partition keys for each tenant to enable multi-tenancy.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Queues messages for asynchronous processing such as tenant setup subroutines and post-check-in customer service or review reminder emails.

edges.notes: Tenant accesses the onboarding web application wizard through the CDN.
CDN routes the tenant wizard request to the AppSync GraphQL gateway.
AppSync resolvers invoke Lambda to fan out to different subroutines.
Lambda places messages into SQS for asynchronous subroutine processing.
SQS messages are reprocessed by Lambda.
Lambda interacts with DynamoDB using tenant partition keys to finish setting up the tenancy.
DynamoDB returns responses to Lambda during tenant setup.
Third-party OTA reseller sends a REST API request through the CDN.
CDN routes third-party reseller traffic to the API Gateway REST endpoint.
API Gateway invokes the shared Lambda functions.
Customer starts their journey on an Anchor website by hitting the CDN.
CDN requests static event descriptions and images from the S3 bucket.
S3 returns the static website assets to the CDN.
CDN returns the static content to the client for browsing and navigation.
Customer requests dynamic booking content or scans a ticket via the mobile check-in app.
CDN routes dynamic and check-in requests to AppSync.
AppSync uses direct DynamoDB resolvers mapped via built-in pipeline resolvers.
AppSync triggers Lambda to process GraphQL nodes for booking and check-in.
Lambda reads and writes booking and check-in state in DynamoDB.
DynamoDB returns booking data to Lambda.
Lambda puts post-check-in messages into SQS for customer service and follow-up actions.
Lambda processes the queued SQS messages to trigger post-experience review reminder emails.
